text:
Predicates:
Employees(x) ::: x is an employee.
SchedulesMeeting(x, y) ::: x schedules a meeting with y.
AppearsInCompany(x) ::: x appears in the company today.
HasLunchInCompany(x) ::: x has lunch in the company.
HasLunchAtHome(x) ::: x has lunch at home.
WorksRemotelyFromHome(x) ::: x works remotely from home.
InOtherCountries(x) ::: x is in another country.
Manager(x) ::: x is a manager.
James ::: James is the individual in question.

Premises:
∀x (SchedulesMeeting(x, y) → AppearsInCompany(x)) ::: All employees who schedule meetings with their customers appear in the company today.
∀x (HasLunchInCompany(x) → SchedulesMeeting(x, y)) ::: Everyone who has lunch in the company schedules meetings with their customers.
∀x (HasLunchInCompany(x) ∨ HasLunchAtHome(x)) ::: Employees either have lunch in the company or at home.
∀x (HasLunchAtHome(x) → WorksRemotelyFromHome(x)) ::: If an employee has lunch at home, then they work remotely from home.
∀x (InOtherCountries(x) → WorksRemotelyFromHome(x)) ::: All employees in other countries work remotely from home.
¬∃x (Manager(x) ∧ WorksRemotelyFromHome(x)) ::: No managers work remotely from home.
James ::: James is either a manager and appears in the company today or neither a manager nor appears in the company today.

Conclusion:
¬HasLunchInCompany(James) ::: James does not have lunch in the company.
